design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: City Design & Construction Manual adopts APWA Section 5600 Default Strategy: Comprehensive Protection — peak control for 1%, 10%, and 50% chance storms plus volumetric/extended detention of the 90% mean annual event. Water quality via MARC/APWA BMP Manual: WQv captures 90% of average annual runoff using 1.37-inch Water Quality Storm for KC metro (WQv = P × Rv).

evidence.excerpt: independent — metro APWA 5600 + MARC BMP standards
In the greater Kansas City Metropolitian area, the Water Quality Storm is the 1.37' rain event.
Example: Design a rain garden to treat runoff from the water quality rainfall event for the Kansas City Metropolitan Area (1.37 inches)
A cap with an orifice or an in-line orifice fitting shall be provided at or near the discharge point of the underdrain system to permit a 40-hr drawdown time for the WQv.
Capture volume shall be sized to treat the WQv and discharge over a period of 40 hours.
captures the water quality volume (WQv) and releases it over a 40-hour period.
verification that the location of bedrock and the seasonal high groundwater table are not closer than three feet from the sub-grade.
A minimum thickness of 12 inches should be used for the aggregate base.
being shallower (approximately 18 inches maximum depth in an EDW main pool versus 6 to 12 feet maximum depth in a EWDB main pool).

extraction_quality.review_notes: Independence D&C Manual / APWA 5600 only on Issuu (no durable direct PDF); criteria from city-cited MARC BMP Manual + published 5600 amendment excerpts.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: KC metro Water Quality Storm is 1.37 inches (WQv captures 90% of average annual runoff). Rain gardens use 12–24 inch amended soil mix and max 6 inch ponding (Section 8.1); bioretention underdrain sized for 40-hour WQv drawdown. Permeable pavement: min 12-inch aggregate base; drawdown design may use 0.5 in/day unless site testing shows higher. EDW permanent pool zones include <6 inch and <18 inch microtopography; EDW main pool max ~18 inches vs EWDB 6–12 ft.
